name: Research Analyst
title: SEBI Registered Research Analyst
intro: From graduation to equity research: NISM Series XV, modelling and valuation skills, an associate role in a research team, then senior analyst, head of research or your own SEBI registration.

phases.title: Graduate
points: A graduate degree in any discipline — SEBI's December 2024 amendments relaxed the earlier requirements.
Strong accounting, maths and writing skills matter most.
Engineers often cover tech and industrial sectors.

phases.title: NISM Series XV
phases.summary: The Research Analyst certification SEBI requires.
points: NISM Series XV: Research Analyst certification is required by SEBI.
Employees publishing research must also hold it.
CFA, FRM or an MBA in finance help in hiring but do not replace the NISM/SEBI requirements.

phases.title: Learn modelling and valuation
phases.summary: Accounting, financial modelling and sector knowledge.
points: Pick a sector and follow it closely.

phases.title: Join a research team
phases.summary: Associate analyst at a brokerage, fund or research firm.
points: Brokerages and research firms hire graduates and MBAs as associate analysts.
Employers: stock brokers, mutual funds, insurers, PMS and AIFs, independent research houses, credit-rating agencies.
As an employee, the firm holds the SEBI registration and you follow its policies.

phases.title: Grow or go independent
phases.summary: Senior analyst, sector head, or your own SEBI registration.
points: Growth path: associate → analyst → senior analyst → head of research / fund manager; owning a sector raises pay.
Independent practice needs SEBI registration under the Research Analysts Regulations, 2014 as amended, with deposit and compliance conditions.
Investment Advisers give personal advice under a different SEBI registration.
